on.places: Srinagar, Dal Lake, Gulmarg, Pahalgam, Sonamarg
on.activities: Pleasant weather and open roads. April brings tulips and blossom, May and June green meadows and the easiest days for Pahalgam and Sonamarg, and September and October clear autumn light. July and August are cool but can bring rain and occasional landslide delays. Shikara rides, houseboats, the Gulmarg gondola, pony rides and valley walks are at their best.

off.activities: Cold, with frost in Srinagar and snow on the hills. Gulmarg is the main draw, with the gondola, sledging and instructor-led skiing, though snow cannot be guaranteed. Heavy snowfall can delay flights and close roads, so Pahalgam and Sonamarg trips may change or be dropped. Pack heavy woollens and keep spare days.

mid.places: Srinagar, Dal Lake, Mughal gardens, Gulmarg, Pahalgam
mid.activities: March brings almond blossom and cold mornings, with snow still on the higher slopes. November brings golden chinar leaves and crisp air, with early snow possible at Gulmarg and short days. Roads to the higher valleys can close after snow, so we confirm the situation before each departure.

profile.overview:
Kashmir is the green valley at the top of India, ringed by the Pir Panjal and Himalayan ranges, with Srinagar, its largest city, at around 1,600 metres. Dal Lake's shikaras and carved wooden houseboats, the terraced Mughal gardens, chinar trees and the pine-lined Lidder river at Pahalgam give it a gentler face than most mountain destinations, while Gulmarg's gondola and the meadows of Sonamarg bring the high Himalaya within a day's drive of the city.

It is a favourite with Indian honeymooners, families and groups, and a classic holiday runs four to six nights. Conditions change with the season: summer is open and green, while winter brings snow and a real chance of flight or road delays. We plan with spare time, check weather and road updates before each departure, and tell you plainly what to expect on your dates.

facts.capital: Srinagar in summer and Jammu in winter (Union Territory of Jammu and Kashmir)
facts.languages: Kashmiri, Urdu, Hindi and English; Dogri in Jammu
facts.climate: Summer days about 20 to 30 degrees Celsius; cool spring and autumn; winter near or below freezing, with snow at Gulmarg and on some days in Srinagar
facts.flight_time: Srinagar (SXR) is usually reached with one stop from Chennai (allow most of a day); Delhi to Srinagar is about 1 hr 30 min. By rail: Jammu Tawi or Katra, then road or rail onward.

reasons.title: Dal Lake and houseboats
reasons.text: Sleep on a carved cedar-wood houseboat and glide past floating gardens in a shikara at sunrise or sunset. It is the most distinctive stay in India.

reasons.title: Mughal gardens
reasons.text: Shalimar Bagh, Nishat Bagh and Chashme Shahi are terraced gardens laid out by Mughal rulers, with chinar trees, fountains and views over the lake.

reasons.title: Four mountain landscapes in one trip
reasons.text: Srinagar's lakes, Gulmarg's meadows and gondola, Pahalgam's river valleys and Sonamarg's high pastures are each a half-day to a day apart.

reasons.title: Snow in the right season
reasons.text: Gulmarg usually holds snow from about December to March, with sledging, skiing lessons and a gondola that climbs close to 4,000 metres. Snow cannot be guaranteed on any date.

reasons.title: Cool summers
reasons.text: From April to October the valley is pleasant when the plains are hot, which makes it a popular family and group escape.

reasons.title: Crafts, saffron and kahwa
reasons.text: Shawls, carpets, papier-mache, walnuts and saffron are all local specialities, best enjoyed with a cup of saffron kahwa.

attractions.title: Dal Lake and shikara rides
attractions.text: Srinagar's famous lake, with houseboats, floating gardens and gentle shikara rides, especially lovely at sunrise and sunset.

attractions.title: Mughal gardens of Srinagar
attractions.text: Shalimar Bagh, Nishat Bagh and Chashme Shahi climb in terraces towards the Zabarwan hills, with the lake below.

attractions.title: Floating vegetable market
attractions.text: An early-morning market where growers sell vegetables from boats on Dal Lake, reached by shikara before sunrise.

attractions.title: Shankaracharya Temple
attractions.text: An ancient hilltop Shiva temple above Srinagar, reached by a flight of steps, with wide views over the city and Dal Lake.

attractions.title: Gulmarg and the Gondola
attractions.text: A high alpine meadow about 50 km from Srinagar. The two-phase gondola rises to close to 4,000 metres, weather permitting.

attractions.title: Pahalgam: Lidder River, Betaab and Aru valleys
attractions.text: A river town among pine forests, with meadow valleys nearby that are reached by short drives or on ponies.

attractions.title: Sonamarg and Thajiwas Glacier
attractions.text: A broad Himalayan valley beside the Sindh river, with the Thajiwas Glacier above it, reached on foot, by pony or by local cab depending on conditions.

experiences.title: A night on a houseboat
experiences.text: Carved cedar-panelled rooms, a lake view and home-cooked meals served on board.

experiences.title: Shikara ride at sunrise or sunset
experiences.text: A slow paddle past lotus beds, floating gardens and the mountains behind the lake.

experiences.title: Gulmarg Gondola
experiences.text: A cable car ride over pine forest and snow slopes to high viewpoints, subject to wind and weather on the day.

experiences.title: Valley walks and pony rides
experiences.text: Gentle walks along the Lidder river at Pahalgam and pony rides to Betaab and Aru valleys, where the road ends.

experiences.title: Snow play and skiing in winter
experiences.text: Sledging, snow walks and instructor-led skiing or snowboarding at Gulmarg, when snow conditions allow.

experiences.title: Shopping for Kashmiri crafts
experiences.text: Pashmina and woollen shawls, carpets, papier-mache, walnut wood, dry fruits and saffron, from established shops in Srinagar.

food.title: Kahwa and noon chai
food.text: Saffron-and-almond green tea (kahwa) and salted pink tea (noon chai) are served everywhere and are best on a cold evening.

food.title: Kashmiri breads
food.text: Crisp bakarkhani, sheermal and girda from Srinagar's bakeries, usually eaten warm with tea for breakfast.

food.title: Wazwan
food.text: The traditional multi-course Kashmiri feast. It is mostly meat-based, so vegetarian guests should ask for the vegetarian dishes instead.

food.title: Vegetarian Kashmiri dishes
food.text: Dum aloo, nadru (lotus stem), haak (leafy greens), rajma and paneer dishes are widely available. We can arrange vegetarian and Jain meal options on request, subject to availability.

food.title: Dry fruits and saffron
food.text: Walnuts, almonds, apricots and Kashmiri saffron make good gifts. Buy from established shops and ask about authenticity.

tips.title: Pack layers for every season
tips.text: Evenings are cool at Gulmarg and Pahalgam even in summer. In winter, bring thermals, a heavy jacket, gloves, a woollen cap and grippy shoes. Snow boots and gear can usually be hired at Gulmarg.

tips.title: Go slowly at altitude
tips.text: Gulmarg's upper gondola station is close to 4,000 metres. Take it easy, drink water and come down if you feel unwell. Speak to a doctor first if you have heart, lung or blood-pressure conditions.

tips.title: Keep spare time in winter
tips.text: Heavy snow or rain can delay flights and close mountain roads, including the Sonamarg and Pahalgam routes. Avoid tight onward connections and tell us if your dates are fixed.

tips.title: Carry cash and check your mobile plan
tips.text: Cards and UPI work in Srinagar, but networks can be patchy in the hills. Prepaid SIMs from other states have often not worked in Jammu and Kashmir, so check with your operator before travelling.

tips.title: Agree rates for ponies and local cabs
tips.text: At Pahalgam, Gulmarg and Sonamarg some points are reached only by pony or local cab. Ask for the official rate list and confirm with us what is included.

tips.title: Buy crafts from established shops
tips.text: Look for the GI label on Kashmir pashmina and saffron, ask for a bill and compare prices before you buy.

travel_info.visa: Indian citizens need no visa for Kashmir. Carry a valid government photo ID such as an Aadhaar card, passport, voter ID or driving licence for every traveller, as hotels and security points ask for it. Srinagar, Gulmarg, Pahalgam and Sonamarg do not generally need a separate permit for Indian visitors, but restricted border areas do. We arrange permits and confirm the current rules at booking.
travel_info.health: No compulsory vaccinations. At Gulmarg's upper gondola station, close to 4,000 metres, some people feel breathless or get a headache, so go slowly and drink water. Carry your regular medicines, as pharmacies and hospitals in the hill towns are basic, and larger hospitals are in Srinagar. Tell us about any heart, lung, blood-pressure or mobility concerns before booking so that we can plan sensibly.
travel_info.money: Cards and UPI work at Srinagar hotels and larger shops, but networks can be patchy at Gulmarg, Pahalgam and Sonamarg, so carry cash for ponies, local cabs, tips and small purchases. ATMs are available in Srinagar and the main towns. Check your mobile plan before you travel, as prepaid connections from other states have often not worked in Jammu and Kashmir.

faqs.q: When is the best time to visit Kashmir?
faqs.a: April to October is the easiest season: spring blossom and tulips in April, green meadows from May to June, and clear autumn light in September and October. December to February is the snow season at Gulmarg, but it is cold and travel can be delayed.

faqs.q: Will there be snow when we travel?
faqs.a: Gulmarg usually has snow from about December to March, sometimes earlier or later, and the amount changes every year, so we cannot guarantee it. Srinagar sees snow only on some winter days. Sonamarg's Thajiwas Glacier often keeps snow into early summer.

Most travellers fly to Srinagar Airport (SXR), usually with one stop from Chennai, often through Delhi. By rail, you can travel to Jammu Tawi or Katra and continue by road, which takes most of a day, or by the new rail link where services suit. We confirm current options at booking.

faqs.q: How many nights do I need?
faqs.a: Five to six nights covers Srinagar, Gulmarg, Pahalgam and Sonamarg without rushing. Four nights from a single Srinagar base works for families, and a three-night weekend break suits Dal Lake and Gulmarg.

faqs.q: Is Kashmir suitable for children and senior parents?
faqs.a: Yes, with a sensible plan. Srinagar and Dal Lake are easy, and we can base you in one hotel with day trips. Gulmarg and Sonamarg involve two to three hours each way, and the upper gondola is at high altitude, so tell us about any health concerns.

Large numbers of Indian travellers visit every year. Conditions can change, so we follow official advisories and local updates, keep to established tourist areas and tell you if anything affects your dates. We also recommend travel insurance.

group_trips.title: Kashmir Valley Group Trip: Dal Lake, Pahalgam, Sonamarg and Gulmarg
group_trips.summary: Seven days in the Kashmir valley with a Dal Lake houseboat, the Mughal gardens, Pahalgam, a day at Sonamarg and the Gulmarg Gondola, with a trip captain.
group_trips.overview:
This fixed-departure group trip covers the best-known places in the Kashmir valley over six nights. You begin with two nights on a houseboat on Dal Lake, with a shikara ride and a day among the Mughal gardens, then drive to Pahalgam for its river and meadow valleys.

From Srinagar you make two day excursions: one to Sonamarg and the Thajiwas Glacier, and one to Gulmarg for the gondola. Day trips from a Srinagar base mean fewer hotel changes, and a trip captain travels with the group throughout. Daily breakfast and dinner are included, and vegetarian and Jain options are available on request.

Mountain roads and the gondola depend on weather, so the order of days may change, and we keep spare time in the plan.
highlights: Two nights on a houseboat on Dal Lake, with a shikara ride
Mughal gardens of Srinagar: Chashme Shahi, Nishat Bagh and Shalimar Bagh
Pahalgam, with Betaab Valley and Aru Valley by local cab
Day trip to Sonamarg and the Thajiwas Glacier area, as conditions allow
Gulmarg Gondola ride (Phase 1 included, Phase 2 optional and weather permitting)
Daily breakfast and dinner, with vegetarian and Jain options on request
Trip captain with the group throughout

itinerary.title: Arrival in Srinagar | Houseboat on Dal Lake | Shikara Ride
itinerary.description:
Arrive at Srinagar Airport, where your trip captain meets the group.
Transfer to your houseboat on Dal Lake and check in.
In the evening, take a shikara ride on the lake, weather permitting.
Dinner on the houseboat.
Overnight stay on Dal Lake, Srinagar.

itinerary.title: Mughal Gardens | Srinagar Sightseeing
itinerary.description:
After breakfast, visit Chashme Shahi, Nishat Bagh and Shalimar Bagh, the terraced Mughal gardens above the lake.
Continue to a local market for shawls, dry fruits and handicrafts, at your own pace.
Spend the evening on the houseboat deck or at leisure.
Overnight stay on Dal Lake, Srinagar.

itinerary.title: Srinagar to Pahalgam | Lidder River
itinerary.description:
After breakfast, check out and drive to Pahalgam, a journey of about three hours.
Check in to your hotel and have a relaxed afternoon.
Walk beside the Lidder river and enjoy the pine-covered slopes.
Overnight stay in Pahalgam.

itinerary.title: Betaab Valley | Aru Valley | Return to Srinagar
itinerary.description:
After breakfast, visit Betaab Valley and Aru Valley by local cab, as local conditions allow.
Pony rides are available at some points and are paid locally.
After lunch at leisure, drive back to Srinagar, about three hours.
Check in to your hotel in Srinagar.
Overnight stay in Srinagar.

itinerary.title: Day Trip to Sonamarg
itinerary.description:
After breakfast, drive to Sonamarg, a journey of about three hours each way.
Enjoy the valley beside the Sindh river and, as conditions allow, the Thajiwas Glacier area by local cab or pony.
Lunch is at your own cost. Return to Srinagar in the evening.
Overnight stay in Srinagar.

itinerary.title: Day Trip to Gulmarg | Gondola
itinerary.description:
After breakfast, drive to Gulmarg, about two hours from Srinagar.
Ride the Gulmarg Gondola (Phase 1 included) and walk across the meadow.
The upper phase is optional and depends on wind and weather on the day.
Return to Srinagar in the late afternoon.
Overnight stay in Srinagar.

itinerary.title: Departure from Srinagar
itinerary.description:
After breakfast, check out of the hotel.
Transfer to Srinagar Airport for your flight home.

group_trips.title: Kashmir Weekend Escape: Dal Lake, Mughal Gardens and Gulmarg
group_trips.summary: A Friday-to-Monday break with a Dal Lake houseboat night, shikara ride, Mughal gardens and a day at Gulmarg with the gondola.
group_trips.overview:
This three-night break fits Kashmir's best-known sights into a long weekend. You spend the first night on a houseboat on Dal Lake, ride a shikara, visit the Mughal gardens and make a day trip to Gulmarg for the gondola.

It is a short programme, so it works best with early arrivals and late departures. A trip captain accompanies every weekly Friday departure, and breakfast and dinner are included.

honeymoon_trips.title: Kashmir Honeymoon: Dal Lake Houseboat, Gulmarg and Pahalgam
honeymoon_trips.summary: Six private nights for two with a Dal Lake houseboat, a sunset shikara ride, the Gulmarg Gondola, Pahalgam's valleys, a couples spa session and a candlelight dinner.
honeymoon_trips.overview:
This private honeymoon starts on the water, with two nights on a houseboat on Dal Lake, then moves to the meadows of Gulmarg and the river valleys of Pahalgam, finishing in Srinagar. You travel by private vehicle, start most mornings unhurried and keep afternoons and evenings for each other.

Expect a flower welcome and bed decoration on arrival, a private shikara ride at sunset, a candlelight dinner and a couples spa session, all subject to availability. Gulmarg to Pahalgam is the longest drive, about five hours with a lunch stop, and we plan it at an easy pace. Tell us your wedding date at booking so that the hotels can prepare the welcome.
highlights: Private vehicle for transfers and sightseeing
Two nights on a Dal Lake houseboat
Private shikara ride at sunset, our signature romantic moment
Gulmarg Gondola ride (Phase 1 included) and a night in the meadows
Pahalgam's Betaab and Aru valleys by local cab
Candlelight dinner and couples spa session, subject to availability
Flower welcome and bed decoration on arrival

custom_trips.title: Kashmir Adventure: Gulmarg Snow or Meadows and Pahalgam Rivers
custom_trips.summary: A private active trip with two nights at Gulmarg for skiing and snow in winter or meadow walks and riding in summer, plus Pahalgam's river and valleys.
custom_trips.overview:
This private adventure trip is built around Gulmarg and Pahalgam, and the activities depend on the season. In winter, usually December to March, Gulmarg offers sledging and instructor-led skiing or snowboarding if snow conditions allow. From late spring to autumn it offers meadow walks, pony rides and views from the gondola.

At Pahalgam you can walk or ride into Aru and Betaab valleys and, in the warmer months, add a river rafting session on the Lidder, subject to water levels. Every plan is quoted for your dates, fitness and group, so ask for a free quote.
